There is one significant and easily observable difference between human male and female dissected brains. The corpus callosum is observably larger in female brains than male brains. This supports the notion of 'female intuition'. This enormous cable connects the 2 brain hemispheres. It has been shown that women are typically able to access disperse data more quickly than men for so-called 'intuitive' answers. However, men with more isolated hemispheres tend to bring more focus to an activity. These studies were carried out in the 1960s and 1970s. So, at least one large and easily measurable structural difference.

Brain size does not matter. This was Broca's research in the 1800s and women have a larger brain to body mass ratio than men, men typically having overall larger brains. Stephen Jay Gould covers this in an essay, "Broca's Brain".

Down to the nitty-gritty. There is a nucleus in the base of the hypothalamus that has a location difference between the genders. The hypothalamus is a roughly thumb sized structure found dorsal (above) the optic chiasm. This part of the brain creates drives - drive to sleep, drive to eat, drive to have sex, with what or whom to have sex etc. Small differences in this area create huge differences in the organismal behavior. In the 1990s and Simon LeVay (doctor in the UK) found a difference in location of a fairly small nucleus at the base of the hypothalamus for men and women. The nuclei (everything is bilateral in the brain, so there are 2) are closer together (either side of the midline) lower (more ventral) in men and more lateral and higher (more dorsal) in women. This difference must be observed after staining and viewing the specimen microscopically. More importantly, the nucleus is found somewhere in between these two "normal" locations for gay men. This is based on some 70 subjects so the observation is not trivial. The upshot of this is that gay men will tend to act, or have drives, similar to both men and women.

This would ordinarily lead to a Nobel Prize type set of accolades however, the doctor himself was gay and all his subjects had AIDS. So, what muddies the waters here is this nucleus shift could be caused by AIDS virus. This research is not much appreciated, however the data holds up.

The issue here, as the Wikipedia article states (check it out - Simon LeVay) that he could not ascertain if the difference was due to genetics. It is very possible that this difference can be due to hormonal control and response, a much more complicated issue than straight (pun not seen ahead of time) genetics.

tl;dr There is at least one significant and easily observable difference between male and female brains. There is also a shown difference between straight male and gay male brains. This difference is small but significant in its location.

Therefore, the premise "research shows that there is actually no difference at all between male and female brains so it's all patriarchy" has been shown to be false.
